rounds.fact: The iTunes Store launched in 2003 selling songs for 99 cents each, a pricing model credited with convincing the music industry that people would actually pay for legal downloads.
GeoCities organized user pages into themed 'neighborhoods' like Hollywood and SiliconValley, and at its peak was one of the most-visited sites on the entire web before Yahoo shut it down in 2009.
LimeWire became one of the most popular peer-to-peer file-sharing programs after Napster's shutdown, before being forced offline itself by a 2010 court injunction.
Newgrounds became the central hub for Flash animation and games in the early 2000s, launching the careers of several animators years before YouTube existed.
Orbitz was launched in 2001 by a group of major airlines banding together to compete directly with Expedia and Travelocity for online bookings.
